name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
region: Tongariro National Park, Central North Island
why: A one-way crossing of an active volcanic massif: up the Mangatepōpō Valley, over the rim of Red Crater at 1,886 m, past the Emerald Lakes and Blue Lake, then down with Lake Taupō in view.
book: Free. DOC recommends that every walker books online (no cost); a booking is required to use a shuttle or a guide. Road-end parking is limited to 4 hours (none for walkers at Mangatepōpō in summer): take a shuttle from National Park Village, Whakapapa or Tūrangi. May-October it is an alpine route: go with a guide.
water: Water along the track is not safe to drink: carry 2-3 litres. Toilets every 1-2 hours.
dangers: Alpine weather all year: strong wind, cold, rain and poor visibility even in summer. DOC posts a "Not Recommended Today" advisory at 06:00 on bad days.
Loose scree on the steep descent from Red Crater to the Emerald Lakes.
Active volcanic area: check the GeoNet alert level. Keep away from steam vents; do not touch or enter the lakes, which are sacred.
May-October: snow, ice and avalanche terrain. Ice axe, crampons, helmet and avalanche gear are needed.
Fires in late 2025 burned the area near the start; a 10-year rāhui covers it: stay on the track.
turnaround: Decide in South Crater, after the climb from the valley: if the wind or cloud is worse than forecast, or you are behind time, walk back to Mangatepōpō.

points.name: Mangatepōpō road end
points.note: Start at 1,120 m. A boardwalk climbs gently up the Mangatepōpō Valley for the first 5.4 km, shared with the Soda Springs Walk.

points.name: Red Crater
points.note: The highest point of the crossing, 1,886 m. On a calm day at least 10 °C colder than Taupō; colder still in wind.

points.name: Ngā Rotopounamu / Emerald Lakes
points.note: Vivid green crater lakes at the foot of the scree descent, with steam vents nearby: keep off the warm ground.

points.name: Blue Lake / Te Wai Whakaata o Te Rangihīroa
points.note: Rangihīroa's mirror, sacred to Ngāti Hikairo. After it the long zigzag descent of the northern slopes begins.

points.name: Ketetahi road end
points.note: End at 760 m after a descent through forest. Shuttles collect here; the private car park is nearby.
